####### # Setup #######
Context('Numeric'); $a = random(2,5); $b = random(1,20); $f = Formula("$a*x + $b"); $start = random(0,10); @x = map{$_ + $start} (0..5); @y = map{$f->eval(x => $_)}(@x); for my $i (0..4) { $diff[$i] = $y[$i+1] - $y[$i]; }; $yes = DropDown(['yes','no'], 0, showInStatic => 0); $no = DropDown(['yes','no'], 1, showInStatic => 0);
############################# # Exercise Group Introduction #############################
BEGIN_PGML Does the table show that [`x`] and [`y`] have a linear relationship?
END_PGML
###### # Body ######
BEGIN_PGML >> [@DataTable( [ [ [PGML('[`x`]'), rowbottom => '2', midrule => '1',], PGML('[`y`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[0]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[0]]`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[1]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[1]]`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[2]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[2]]`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[3]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[3]]`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[4]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[4]]`]'), ], [ PGML('[`[$x[5]]`]'), PGML('[`[$y[5]]`]'), ], ], align => '*{2}{r}', valign => 'middle',);@]* <<
[_]{$no}{5}
END_PGML
########## # Solution ##########
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION As each [`x`]-value increases by [`1\text{,}`] the [`y`]-values increases by [`[$diff[0]]\text{,}`] then [`[$diff[1]]\text{,}`] then [`[$diff[2]]\text{,}`] then [`[$diff[3]]\text{,}`] then [`[$diff[4]]\text{.}`] So this table shows that [`x`] and [`y`] do not have a linear relationship.
END_PGML_SOLUTION
